cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine prepare the quarterly review of HANGS Construction Services.
A review is lighter than an audit: questions and comparisons, not full testing.
Materiality, the size of error that matters, is $100,000 here.
Revenue is up, but the margin fell.
The controller answers every question in writing.
Now it rebuilds each job's revenue from its costs, and it ties to the books.
One job's profit fell after its cost estimate rose.
Then it rebuilds the quarter's interest from each loan.
Interest is booked only when paid, so $35,350 is missing.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft review memo for the CPA.

All done. Interest expense is $6,685 short, well under materiality. The bigger question is a $259,200 change order the customer has not signed, which also decides whether net worth still meets the loan covenant. Ten items stay open. This is not a review report: the CPA, a person, concludes and signs.
